title: Proposal to Include Telecommunications Operators’ Call Centres in Regulator's Quality of Service Standards
what_it_is: Proposal to Include Telecommunications Operators’ Call Centres in Regulator's Quality of Service Standards

sections.label: IMDA Quality of Service standards
sections.summary: IMDA sets minimum Quality of Service standards for key telecommunication services, verifies compliance and enforces breaches, but imposes no regulatory requirements on customer service and call centres.

sentences.text: The following question stood in the name of Mr Murali Pillai 	–  34 To ask the Minister for Communications and Information whether the Quality of Service standards imposed by IMDA on its regulated telecommunications operators may be expanded to cover the management of these operators' call centres which are contracted to deal with and resolve subscribers' requests for assistance and complaints.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: So, IMDA sets minimum Quality of Service (QoS) standards for the performance of these key telecommunication services, such as fixed line telephone, mobile, Internet access and fibre connection services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: IMDA regularly verifies service providers' compliance with these QoS standards and takes enforcement action in the event of breaches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: IMDA does not impose regulatory requirements on customer service and call centre experiences.

sections.label: Consumer satisfaction with telecommunication providers
sections.summary: CASS 2018 showed consumers are generally satisfied with their telecommunication service providers, with improvement in hotline waiting time, complaint resolution time and customer service officer competency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: CASS 2018 showed that consumers are generally satisfied with their telecommunication service providers, and consumer satisfaction has improved in several areas, including the hotline waiting time, time taken to resolve complaints, and competency of service providers’ customer service officers.
